authorship: MANUAL specification written by the researcher/coder for the T01 fixture. It encodes intended protocol policy and is not derived or verified from any circuit or contract.

activation.otherwise: evidence_error (the T01 circuit constrains flags to Boolean, so any other authenticated value is not a valid statement)

depositIdentity.batchId: keccak256 over the concatenation of the ten public inputs, each as a 32-byte big-endian word, in index order (equals keccak256(abi.encode(uint256[10])))

obligation: For a successful settlement, every active row i must have, before the call, a funded escrow entry for (batchId, i) with amount == publicInputs[amount[i]] * weiPerUnit and consumed == false, and that entry must be consumed after the call. The sum of newly consumed entry amounts must equal the change in consumedBacking. Pre/post commitments must equal the authenticated old/new commitments. A reverted settlement must leave all observed protected state unchanged.
assumptions: Proof acceptance is INFERRED, not observed. A recorded verifier call whose calldata carries the settlement's public inputs, together with a successful outer call, establishes that the proof was accepted ONLY IF the consumer enforces the verifier's boolean result (reverts when it returns false). That enforcement is not visible in an execution record and must be confirmed separately for every evaluated consumer (T07 does this by code excerpt and a behavioral test). The verifier's return value itself is not captured by the recording mechanism.
State is observed only for the escrow rows of the recorded batch identity, the commitment, the backing counter and the consumer's ETH balance. Other batches, events and token flows are not observed.
